These pathways indicate that the compound may influence VEGFR3 through multiple intermediate steps, potentially via the regulation of Geminin or NIM1.

The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the pathways are derived from a single dataset and may not fully capture the complexity of the biological system. The integration of these pathways highlights the potential for the compound to exert a regulatory effect on VEGFR3, though the precise nature of this effect remains to be determined.
